# New York No-Heat Tenant Action Plan

You have a strong paper trail already: lease start on **2025-11-01**, written notice on **2026-01-08**, indoor temperature around **15°C**, and **3 ignored follow-ups**. The safest next move is to keep everything in writing, document the habitability problem, and prepare for city/legal escalation if the landlord still does nothing.

# Tenant Checklist, Email Draft, and Records to Save

## Tenant-friendly steps to take now
- Keep measuring and logging the indoor temperature at different times of day.
- Take dated photos or short videos of the thermostat, thermometer, and any visible heater problem.
- Send one final written notice asking for repair by a specific deadline.
- If heat is still not restored, contact **311 / NYC Housing Preservation & Development** to report a heat/hot water complaint.
- If the apartment is unsafe or the temperature drops further, consider local tenant legal aid or housing court options.
- Do not stop paying rent unless you get legal advice first; instead, preserve your rights with documentation.

## Polite but firm email template
Subject: Urgent Repair Request — Broken Heater at [Apartment Address]

Dear [Landlord/Property Manager Name],

I am writing again about the broken heater in my apartment at [address]. I first reported this issue in writing on **2026-01-08**, and I have sent **three follow-up emails** since then. The problem remains unresolved, and the indoor temperature has been around **15°C**, which is not a safe or habitable condition.

Please arrange for the heater to be repaired immediately and confirm in writing when a technician will be coming. If possible, I would appreciate a response by **[insert date/time, such as 24 hours from now]**.

For reference, my lease began on **2025-11-01**, and I have kept records of the issue, including temperatures and prior communications.

Thank you for your prompt attention to this matter. I look forward to your written confirmation.

Sincerely,
[Your full name]
[Apartment number]
[Phone number]
[Email address]

## Documents and evidence to keep
- Lease and any amendments or addenda
- Your first written complaint from **2026-01-08**
- All 3 follow-up emails, with sent dates and any delivery/read receipts
- Any landlord replies, even brief ones
- Temperature logs showing date, time, and reading
- Photos or videos of the broken heater, thermostat, and thermometer
- Any repair appointment notices, cancellations, or missed visits
- Utility bills if the heater issue affected costs
- Notes of phone calls: date, time, person spoken to, and what was said
- A copy of your rent payment history
- Any messages from neighbors about the same issue, if relevant

## Quick Actions
Action: [Button: File 311 complaint](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/)
Action: [Button: NYC tenant help](https://www.nyc.gov/site/hpd/services-and-information/tenants-rights.page)
Action: [Button: Legal aid finder](https://www.legalservicesnyc.org/)

## Sources
- NYC 311 housing complaints: https://portal.311.nyc.gov/
- NYC HPD tenants’ rights: https://www.nyc.gov/site/hpd/services-and-information/tenants-rights.page
- Legal Services NYC: https://www.legalservicesnyc.org/
